task_summary: Implement the App Shell, Routing & Layout component for a Vite + React 18 + Convex application in TypeScript. This includes: Convex client initialization, React Router v6 route configuration, a sidebar-based layout with navigation, slug validation/path generation utilities, and fade-in animation keyframes. The component must integrate with a data layer dependency and follow strict TypeScript/Tailwind/Bun conventions.

findings.finding: Convex provides `ConvexReactClient` from 'convex/react' which should be instantiated once at the module level (outside React tree), then passed to `<ConvexProvider client={client}>` wrapping the app. The URL comes from `VITE_CONVEX_URL` env var. The client must NOT be created inside a component to avoid re-instantiation on re-renders. Type the return as `ConvexReactClient`.
findings.relevance: Directly implements createConvexClient(). Must use ConvexProvider, not ConvexProviderWithClerk or similar auth wrappers unless auth is specified.

findings.finding: Use `<Outlet />` inside a layout route component. Define routes with `createBrowserRouter` or nested `<Route>` elements where the layout route wraps child routes. The layout component renders persistent UI (sidebar, header) plus `<Outlet />` for page content. This is the canonical v6 pattern replacing v5's render props.
findings.relevance: Directly implements renderLayout() and the RoutesObject. The sidebar persists across route changes while Outlet swaps page content.

findings.topic: Sidebar Navigation with React Router v6
findings.finding: Use `useNavigate()` or `<NavLink>` for sidebar items. `<NavLink>` provides automatic `isActive` styling via className callback: `className={({isActive}) => ...}`. For programmatic navigation (onNavigate callback), `useNavigate()` returns a function. Use `useLocation()` or `useParams()` to derive currentSlug for active state highlighting.
findings.relevance: Implements renderSidebar() with currentSlug tracking and onNavigate callback. NavLink is preferred for accessibility (renders <a> tags) but onNavigate prop suggests programmatic control.

findings.finding: Use a string literal union type or `as const` object for ToolSlug rather than a TypeScript `enum` to maintain tree-shakeability and better type inference. Validation function `isValidToolSlug` should use a type guard: `(value: string): value is ToolSlug`. Path generation `toolPath` should return a template literal like `/tools/${slug}`.
findings.source: TypeScript handbook + community best practices (Matt Pocock, Total TypeScript)
findings.relevance: Directly implements ToolSlug type, isValidToolSlug(), and toolPath(). Type guard pattern enables narrowing in consuming code.

findings.finding: Vite exposes env vars prefixed with `VITE_` via `import.meta.env`. For TypeScript, extend `ImportMetaEnv` in a `vite-env.d.ts` file to type `VITE_CONVEX_URL: string`. Without this, `import.meta.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL` is `string | undefined` and requires runtime assertion.
findings.relevance: Required for createConvexClient() to safely read the Convex deployment URL. Missing type declaration is a common pitfall causing TS errors.

findings.finding: Define custom keyframes in `tailwind.config.ts` under `theme.extend.keyframes` and reference them in `theme.extend.animation`. Pattern: `keyframes: { fadeIn: { '0%': { opacity: '0' }, '100%': { opacity: '1' } } }, animation: { 'fade-in': 'fadeIn 300ms ease-in-out' }`. Then use `animate-fade-in` class in JSX.
findings.relevance: Directly implements FadeInKeyframes type and the Tailwind animation config. Avoids custom CSS per project standards.

findings.finding: Add `<link>` tags in `index.html` for Google Fonts, then reference the font family in `tailwind.config.ts` under `theme.extend.fontFamily`. Alternatively use `@fontsource` packages for self-hosted fonts. The GoogleFontLink type suggests the index.html approach with preconnect to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com.
findings.source: Google Fonts API docs + Vite static HTML conventions
findings.relevance: Implements GoogleFontLink and TailwindFontConfig types. Preconnect links improve font loading performance.

findings.finding: 1) ConvexProvider must wrap RouterProvider/BrowserRouter, not vice versa, so Convex hooks work in all route components. 2) Do not use `React.lazy()` for the layout component itself—only for page-level components—to avoid layout flash. 3) Convex subscriptions auto-reconnect but initial load shows undefined; handle loading states. 4) StrictMode double-invokes effects; ensure ConvexReactClient is created outside the component tree.
findings.source: Convex community patterns, React 18 StrictMode docs
findings.relevance: Critical architectural ordering for renderApp(). Wrong provider nesting is the #1 integration bug.

findings.finding: Recommended structure: `src/main.tsx` (entry, createConvexClient, renderApp), `src/App.tsx` (router setup), `src/components/Layout.tsx` (renderLayout with Outlet), `src/components/Sidebar.tsx` (renderSidebar), `src/lib/routes.ts` (ToolSlug, isValidToolSlug, toolPath, RoutesObject), `src/lib/convex.ts` (client creation). Keep each file under 300 lines per project standards.
findings.relevance: Satisfies the 300-line file limit and separation of concerns. Each function maps cleanly to a file.

findings.finding: Sidebar should use `<nav>` landmark with `aria-label='Tool navigation'`. Active item should have `aria-current='page'`. Use semantic `<a>` or `<NavLink>` elements, not `<div onClick>`. Keyboard navigation (Tab, Enter) works automatically with anchor elements. Color contrast for active vs inactive items must meet WCAG 2.1 AA (4.5:1 ratio).
findings.relevance: Sidebar rendering must be accessible. HexColorString type suggests custom colors—must verify contrast ratios.

findings.topic: Performance: Code Splitting with React Router v6
findings.finding: Use `React.lazy()` + `<Suspense>` for route-level code splitting. In React Router v6, this is done by lazy-loading the component prop of each `<Route>`. Alternatively, use the `lazy` property on route objects with `createBrowserRouter`. This keeps the app shell bundle small while loading tool pages on demand.
findings.source: React Router v6 lazy loading docs
findings.relevance: Important for scalability as more tools are added. The ToolSlug enum implies multiple tool pages that benefit from code splitting.

recommended_approach:
**Architecture:**

1. **`src/lib/convex.ts`** — `createConvexClient()` as a singleton factory reading `import.meta.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL`. Returns `ConvexReactClient`. Guard against missing env var with a runtime assertion.

2. **`src/lib/routes.ts`** — Define `ToolSlug` as a `const` object with derived union type. Implement `isValidToolSlug()` as a type guard checking against the known slug set. Implement `toolPath()` returning `/tools/${slug}`. Export `RoutesObject` type and route configuration.

3. **`src/main.tsx`** — `renderApp()`: Create the Convex client, wrap `<React.StrictMode><ConvexProvider><BrowserRouter><App /></BrowserRouter></ConvexProvider></React.StrictMode>`, call `createRoot().render()`.

4. **`src/components/Layout.tsx`** — `renderLayout()`: Flex container with `<Sidebar>` on the left and `<Outlet />` on the right. Apply `animate-fade-in` to the outlet wrapper for page transitions.

5. **`src/components/Sidebar.tsx`** — `renderSidebar()`: `<nav>` element with mapped `SidebarItem[]`. Use `NavLink` for each item, derive active state from React Router. `projectToolDefToSidebarItem()` maps data layer tool definitions to `SidebarItem` shape.

6. **`tailwind.config.ts`** — Extend with `fadeIn` keyframes, custom font family, and any HexColor tokens.

7. **`index.html`** — Google Font `<link>` tags with preconnect.

**Key decisions:**
- ConvexProvider wraps BrowserRouter (outer position) so all routed components access Convex.
- Derive currentSlug from `useParams()` rather than prop-drilling, reducing state sync bugs.
- Singleton pattern for Convex client to support both app and test contexts.
- Type guard `isValidToolSlug` enables safe slug validation at route boundaries (e.g., a catch-all route param).
alternatives_considered: createBrowserRouter (data router) vs <BrowserRouter> (JSX router): Data router supports v6.4+ features (loaders, actions, deferred data) but adds complexity. Since Convex handles data fetching reactively via hooks, the simpler <BrowserRouter> + <Routes> JSX approach is sufficient and more idiomatic with Convex. Recommend <BrowserRouter> unless loader-based data fetching is needed.

Module-level Convex client vs context-based factory: Module-level singleton is simpler and recommended by Convex docs. A factory function (createConvexClient) allows testing/mocking. Recommend: factory function that caches the instance (singleton pattern) so tests can reset it.

String union vs TypeScript enum for ToolSlug: String union is more idiomatic modern TS, tree-shakeable, and works better with type guards. However, the spec says 'enum'. Recommend: const object with `as const` + derived union type, which gives enum-like namespacing while remaining a string union at the type level.

Sidebar state management: Could use React Router's location as single source of truth (derived state) vs maintaining separate currentSlug state. Recommend deriving from useLocation/useParams to avoid state synchronization bugs.
risks: VITE_CONVEX_URL not set in environment — createConvexClient() will fail silently or throw. Must add runtime validation with a clear error message.

ToolSlug enum drift — if data_layer adds new tools but ToolSlug is not updated, routes will 404. Consider deriving ToolSlug from the data layer's tool definitions if possible, or add a build-time check.
Sidebar re-renders on every navigation if not memoized. Use React.memo on Sidebar and ensure SidebarItem[] reference stability (useMemo on the mapping).
Google Fonts blocking render — <link> tags in <head> are render-blocking. Use `font-display: swap` (default for Google Fonts API v2) and add `preconnect` to mitigate.
React Router v6 nested route matching — trailing slashes and case sensitivity can cause route mismatches. Normalize slugs to lowercase and configure consistent trailing slash behavior.
Convex client WebSocket connection in development with StrictMode — double effect invocation may cause brief double-connection. ConvexReactClient handles this gracefully but worth noting.
compliance_notes: All files must be .ts or .tsx — no .js, .jsx, or .py files
Package manager is Bun only — all install commands use `bun add`, scripts use `bun run`
Dev server must run on port 4000 — configure in vite.config.ts: server: { port: 4000 }
Tailwind CSS v3 for all styling — no custom CSS unless absolutely necessary (fade-in keyframes go in tailwind.config.ts, not a CSS file)
React functional components only with TypeScript interfaces for props
Type annotations required on all exported functions and components
Files must stay under 300 lines — split Layout and Sidebar into separate files
React Router v6 for all routing — no other router libraries
Tests must be runnable with vitest
